variants.name: Spring MVC: ContentNegotiatingViewResolver over a ViewResolver chain
variants.implementation_notes: Spring MVC resolves the representation, not the handler: the controller returns a model with a logical view name and ContentNegotiatingViewResolver asks its ContentNegotiationManager for the requested media types (Accept header by default; the query-parameter strategy is preferred over path extensions), then polls each delegate ViewResolver - Thymeleaf, InternalResourceViewResolver for JSP, Jackson for JSON, a PDF view - and returns the first View whose content type is compatible. The resolver chain is the classic view registry and the negotiation manager is the selection logic; only a genuinely new format (CSV, iCal) needs a hand-written View. Enabling setUseNotAcceptableStatusCode(true) turns an unmatched request into an explicit 406 instead of a null view.
pitfalls: ContentNegotiatingViewResolver must be ordered ahead of the other resolvers (Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE); otherwise the JSP resolver wins and JSON clients receive HTML with 200.
Path-extension negotiation is discouraged by Spring's own documentation (suffix matching and RFD); prefer the Accept header or a query parameter so URLs stay cacheable.
defaultViews are only candidates: each still has to satisfy the requested content type, so a missing default silently yields the first compatible view.

variants.name: Jakarta REST: @Produces with several media types
variants.implementation_notes: In Jakarta REST the representation is declared on the resource method: one @GET annotated with several media types in @Produces lets the runtime pick the matching MessageBodyWriter from the Accept header, so the method returns the same model object and JSON, XML or a custom media type are produced by the registered providers - the provider registry is the view registry and the annotation is the negotiation declaration. Choose this when the application is already REST-annotated and you want representation choice visible at the method, without the resolver-chain indirection of a servlet MVC stack.
pitfalls: Adding a media type to @Produces without a registered MessageBodyWriter/Provider for it fails at runtime (500 or 406), not at compile time.
A DTO that must serve JSON and XML needs both annotation sets and (for JAXB) a no-arg constructor; annotating the JPA entity instead lets lazy relations explode outside the transaction.
Media type parameters and q-values are matched by the runtime, so an over-broad @Produces("*/*") silently makes the framework pick for you and hides regressions.
